one_liner: Block-STM parallel executor for whole EVM blocks on top of revm; about 2x sequential revm on mainnet blocks.
what_it_does: Executes all transactions of an Ethereum (or RISE) block across worker threads and returns the same per-transaction receipts and state transitions as sequential execution. The API is block-level: Pevm::execute takes an alloy Block (or execute_revm_parallel takes a Vec<TxEnv>) plus a read-only Storage implementation and a thread count; the caller commits the returned state and computes the state root itself. VM execution is still delegated to revm; pevm only schedules, detects conflicts and re-executes.
how_it_is_fast: Optimistic concurrency in the style of Block-STM: transactions run speculatively against a multi-version memory (a DashMap from location hash to a BTreeMap of per-transaction writes), and a collaborative scheduler hands out execution and validation tasks, re-executing transactions whose read set was invalidated. EVM-specific tweaks remove the most common false conflicts: gas payments to the block beneficiary and simple ETH transfers between already-touched accounts are recorded as lazy balance deltas and only evaluated after the block, so every transaction does not depend on the coinbase account. Smaller tricks include identifying locations by a precomputed 64-bit hash, a per-slot UnsafeCell result buffer, and freeing the multi-version memory on a background thread.
when_to_use: Syncing or building large EVM blocks (roughly 10M gas and up) on a many-core server: the 2024 tables show 1.5-3.7x on most London-to-Cancun mainnet blocks, and 22 Cancun-era rows have a geometric mean of 1.92x (derived from page data).

App-specific chains or L2s whose blocks are dominated by transactions touching disjoint state (many independent swaps or token transfers), where the mocked 1-Gigagas blocks reach 4.05x (ERC20) to 22.1x (Uniswap) on 32 vCPUs.
Rust node stacks already built on revm and alloy (reth-style) that can expose a Send + Sync read-only state snapshot and want results bit-identical to sequential execution.
Research on parallel EVM scheduling: the repo calls itself a playground for Parallel EVM R&D and ships mainnet block snapshots plus mocked-block benchmarks to compare against.
when_not_to_use: Small or highly interdependent blocks: blocks under 4,000,000 gas or with fewer transactions than threads fall back to sequential revm (18 of 85 mainnet rows at 1.0x), and 4 of 85 rows are slower (0.89x to 0.93x); a block that self-destructs and redeploys a contract aborts the parallel run and starts over sequentially.

Production consensus or block building with untrusted transactions: the README says work in progress and not production ready, issue #518 (EIP-7702 re-delegation leaves a stale code hash, so parallel diverges from sequential) is open with its fix PR #519 unmerged, and the retry path for insufficient-funds or nonce-too-high transactions is commented as able to deadlock on new or faulty blocks.
Single-thread or per-transaction latency work: pevm still runs the stock revm interpreter for each transaction, so a faster interpreter or compiler (revmc, evmone) is the tool for that.
If you need the state root or disk-backed state: state-root calculation (sparse trie) is still TODO, and all published numbers preload the block's pre-state into memory.
If you need a stable published crate: crates.io has only pevm 0.1.0 from 2024-05-28, so current code has to be taken as a git dependency.

integration.form: crate (git dependency; the crates.io release 0.1.0 dates from 2024-05-28)
integration.dependencies: revm 38, op-revm 19, alloy 2.x crates (consensus, primitives, provider, rpc-types-eth, trie, rlp), op-alloy, dashmap, hashbrown, rustc-hash, smallvec, bitflags, thiserror, serde; optional reqwest, tokio and alloy-transport (rpc-storage feature) and rpmalloc, snmalloc-rs, tikv-jemallocator (global-alloc feature; snmalloc needs cmake)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2024 (rustc 1.85 or newer); no rust-version field or rust-toolchain file
integration.platforms: Any Rust target with std threads; numbers are from aarch64 (Graviton3). The mainnet bench caps threads at 12 on aarch64 and 8 elsewhere, and the bench README says rpmalloc can crash on Graviton.
integration.thread_safety: Pevm::execute takes &mut self, so one block at a time per Pevm instance; each call spawns concurrency_level scoped OS threads, and each instance keeps one background thread for deferred drops. Storage must be Send + Sync.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it wraps revm rather than replacing it: a block-level call over its own read-only Storage trait that returns per-transaction receipts and state transitions for the caller to commit; Ethereum and RISE chain specs only (OP support was replaced by RISE in April 2026).

gotchas: The published tables come from the November 2024 code (tables last changed in commit 82fd0f1, 2024-11-05), which defined the NeedValidation bitflag as 0, so every transaction was always validated. PR #508 fixed this on 2026-05-26, and the maintainer's open issue #509 says the corrected code is slower than the buggy version, without figures. HEAD therefore probably does not reproduce the tables. That 2024 run used the risechain/revm fork at rev 7345c07, ran gigagas under SpecId::LATEST rather than the CANCUN the README states, and had panic=abort in the release profile already.

Harness details that favour the parallel column. The sequential baseline is pevm's own execute_revm_sequential, which deep-clones each transaction's state for CacheDB::commit and frees the CacheDB inside the timed call. The parallel path hands its MvMemory and Scheduler (and in 2024 the transaction vector) to a background AsyncDropper thread, so that deallocation falls outside the timing. The gigagas blocks are independent by construction: raw and ERC20 transfers are self-transfers, and every Uniswap swap gets its own tokens, pool and router. The 'average 2.02x' is a ratio of summed times (report.py); the per-block geometric mean is 1.78x (derived from page data).

Correctness risk, found by reading the code and not demonstrated: memory locations in the multi-version memory, read sets and write sets are identified only by an unkeyed 64-bit FxHash of (address, slot). If two storage slots read and written in one block collide, a later read silently returns the other slot's value. A contract can pick its own slot indices, so a collision found by a birthday search (about 2^32 hashes) could make parallel results diverge from sequential ones on purpose. The code's TODO considers only the performance effect of collisions.

The gigagas bench dropped each run's Result unchecked until commit 00c6928 (2026-05-19), which added nonce: 1 and .expect(). Raw-transfer runs after the April 2026 revm bumps probably errored on the first transaction, inferred from the diff and not run. The 2024 numbers are not affected: that revm fork's TxEnv nonce was Option and None skips the check. The scheduler spin-waits with thread::yield_now, so speedup depends on the OS scheduler: the 2024-11-05 bench README reported a large slowdown on Linux 6.8 (EEVDF) before replacing that note with a warning that mixing efficiency cores costs over 25%. The benchmark machine's kernel is not stated.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick pevm when whole-block throughput on many cores is the bottleneck and blocks have real transaction-level independence. revm (its own baseline), evmone, evm2 and Guillotine make each transaction faster on one core, and revmc compiles hot contracts, so those help even on fully serial blocks. pevm still calls revm for each transaction, so the two approaches are complementary; no combined numbers are documented. A Supra AFT 2025 paper (seen only as a search snippet) reports its conflict-specification executor up to 1.33x faster than PEVM on synthetic workloads.
verified_claims_summary: Criterion (100 samples) on an AWS c7g.8xlarge (Graviton3, 32 vCPUs), November 2024 code, rustc version not stated, release profile with fat LTO and codegen-units=1. The baseline is revm run sequentially through pevm's own execute_revm_sequential over in-memory pre-state. Results: 85 Frontier-to-Cancun mainnet blocks at 2.04x by summed time and 1.78x geometric mean (max 4.32x, min 0.89x) with up to 12 threads and snmalloc; mocked 1-Gigagas blocks with 32 threads and jemalloc THP at 2.82x (raw transfers), 4.05x (ERC20) and 22.1x (Uniswap).
status_note: Active (last commit 2026-06-05) and MIT-licensed, but self-described as work in progress and not production ready. The published numbers predate the NeedValidation fix, which the maintainer says is slower, and the revm 22-to-38 bumps. An EIP-7702 divergence bug (#518) is open, and the code read here shows a 64-bit hash-collision correctness risk; treat it as a research executor to benchmark yourself, not a drop-in node component.
